newsitem.title: PERU: Peru archeologists find meteorites at Machu Picchu.
newsitem.headline: Peru archeologists find meteorites at Machu Picchu.

text.p: Peruvian archaeologists have found a pair of tiny meteorites in the ruins of the ancient city of Machu Picchu, an important religious centre of the pre-Colombian Inca empire.

The meteorites, found among a collection of carvings, rings, collars and other utensils, are thought to have been used by the Incas to hew stone and metal and suggest that the site was not only a religous centre but a working city.

"The discovery of these meteorites, which were used as tools, confirms the hypothesis that Machu Picchu was used every day as a working city," said Elba Torres, who is in charge of the archaeological investigations in Machu Picchu.

The meteorites were no bigger than two inches (five cm) in diameter and were black with a reddish tone. "These are known in Quechua (the Inca language) as 'siguaros' and are of meteorite origin. They are metals used by the Incas to work stones," Torres said.

A lot of meteorites have been found in the Andean region surrounding Cuzco, the former capital of the Inca empire about 60 miles (100 km) south of Machu Picchu. Machu Picchu was discovered in 1912 by U.S. archaeologist Hiram Bingham and was proclaimed a World Heritage Site by UNESCO in 1983. It is one of Latin America's most popular tourist attractions.
